drug_class: HER2-targeted monoclonal antibody (combined with a permeation enhancer)
purpose: This medication is used to treat certain types of breast cancer and stomach cancer that have too much of a protein called HER2 on their cancer cells. It helps stop the cancer from growing and spreading. Your doctor will have tested your tumor to confirm it is HER2-positive before prescribing this medicine.
how_it_works: Think of HER2 as a switch on cancer cells that tells them to grow rapidly. Trastuzumab is a man-made antibody that attaches to that switch and turns it off, slowing or stopping cancer cell growth. The hyaluronidase part is like a helper ingredient that loosens the tissue under your skin so the medication can be absorbed quickly and reach your bloodstream.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include injection site reactions like redness, pain, or swelling under the skin, fatigue or tiredness, nausea, headache, muscle or joint aches, and increased chance of infections. Many patients also experience hair thinning.
warnings: This medication can sometimes weaken the heart, so your doctor will check your heart function regularly. It should never be used during pregnancy as it can seriously harm an unborn baby — please use reliable birth control and tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Some patients may have serious allergic or infusion-related reactions, especially during or after the first few doses. Tell your doctor immediately if you feel short of breath, have chest pain, or notice swelling.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as a shot under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in the thigh or belly area, by a healthcare professional in a clinic or hospital. It is typically given once every 3 weeks. The injection usually takes just 2 to 5 minutes, which is much faster than an IV infusion. Your doctor will decide how long you need to continue treatment based on your specific situation.
